> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a3aa4d291416b57bfe7e89be44f35e7244c5d41f` — the merge of head `aea174380649ef644be6fdf068f05453079a715a` into base `fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a3aa4d291416b57bfe7e89be44f35e7244c5d41f && git checkout a3aa4d291416b57bfe7e89be44f35e7244c5d41f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 aea174380649ef644be6fdf068f05453079a715a && git checkout -B drift-repro fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 && git merge --no-ff aea174380649ef644be6fdf068f05453079a715a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the record below. It was rendered on this head at the contract-review tier by an isolated reviewer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aea174380649ef644be6fdf068f05453079a715a`
Local-runs: probe — one throwaway worktree at the head (since removed; the shared clone was untouched) to run the rule files and the ablations. What it ran:
- `invitation-acceptance-verified-address`, `audience-posture` and `presented-invitation`: 121 passed.
- Ablation with the `email_domain` arm answering no: 4 red. Restored.
- Ablation with it answering yes for every invitation-admitted sign-up: 2 red. Restored.
- Ablation with the `invite_only` arm answering no: 6 red. Restored.
- `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-empty-changeset`: exit 0.

The reviewer did not run the full suites, dogfood, the workspace type check, the derived gates or CI.

Scope: net diff `28a733e55f..aea1743806` (10 files, +307 −30), the PR body, and `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` at this head, which the PR does not edit.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rule is enforced on every door of the ruled class.**
  - `isAdmittedByInvitationAlone` (`audience-posture.ts:551-563`) answers yes under `email_domain` for a self-serve creation off the allowlist that a pending invitation admitted.
  - `validateAudienceAdmission` (`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts:325`) stages it on the creating request. The settle seams are unchanged.
  - A password sign-up and a provider-made account whose address the provider did not verify are both left unbound; both are pinned.
  - A creation whose own flow proves the mailbox binds, as intended (pinned).
- **The `invite_only` arm** behaves exactly like the flag it replaces. The earlier cases stay green and turn red under ablation.
- **Over-refusal: none found.** These cases still bind, and each is pinned:
  - an address on the allowlist, invited or not;
  - an operator-provisioned address off the allowlist;
  - the first account.
- **Docs.**
  - `self-hosting.mdx:763-770`, `tenancy-modes.mdx:246-253`, `environment-variables.mdx:100` and `authentication.mdx:125-130` are accurate.
  - `sso.mdx` is not falsified: its `email_domain` statements concern admission through a registered provider and proven-domain verification, not binding.
- **PR body:** accurate against the diff.

**Findings**

- **S1 (not blocking; predates this PR; narrows only).** For an address on the allowlist that also holds a pending invitation, the admission verdict and the binding decision classify the same sign-up differently. The changeset's "admitted by its domain, invitation or not" is true of binding only. Filed as follow-up card #34971.
- **N1.** The on-allowlist control asserts the membership, not the permission-set grant. This is carried by #34971.
- **N2.** The landing order against ADR amendment #34909 is with the maintainer.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` is correct.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` are truthful. No export of a published entry changes.
- The BREAKING banner, `!`, "What to do" and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are all present.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path is touched.
- ADR-0093's pending amendment names `invite_only` only. Widening it is with the maintainer.
- A separate matter on a neighbouring surface, unchanged by this PR, is recorded with the security seat. [detail held by the security seat]

### ④ Design judgment

One pure decision, read by both postures and staged on the existing request-scoped record with the settle seams untouched, is the smallest correct shape. The cost is the S1 asymmetry, which is better fixed in the verdict (#34971) than by widening this rule.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-q2gv-domain`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
